What is EMI?: EMI stands for Equated Monthly Installment. It is the fixed amount you pay back to the bank every month until your loan is fully paid off, consisting of both principal and interest components.
How is EMI calculated?: EMI is calculated using the formula: EMI = [P x R x (1+R)^N] / [(1+R)^N - 1], where P is Principal, R is monthly interest rate, and N is tenure in months.
What is an EMI calculator?: An EMI calculator is an online tool that helps you estimate your monthly payment by entering the loan amount, interest rate, and tenure.
What is the maximum repayment tenure for: The maximum repayment tenure for a Home Loan is 30 years, subject to the applicant's retirement age.
The maximum repayment tenure for an unsecured Personal Loan is 5 years (60 months).
The maximum repayment tenure for a new Vehicle Loan is 7 years (84 months).
What is a moratorium period?: A moratorium period is a temporary holiday during which you are not required to make payments, common in education and agricultural loans.
Does interest accrue during a moratorium: Yes, interest continues to accrue on the outstanding principal balance during the moratorium period, which increases the total cost of the loan.
What is a grace period?: A grace period is an extra time window (usually 3 to 5 days) allowed to pay your monthly installment after the due date without late fees.
What are the modes of EMI payment?: You can pay EMIs via Auto-Debit (NACH mandate), standing instructions on your savings account, Net Banking, or UPI payments.
What are EMI bounce charges?: EMI bounce charges are penalties (usually ₹250 to ₹500) levied by both your bank and the lending bank if your account has insufficient funds on the EMI date.
What is the late payment fee?: A late fee is a charge (typically 2% per month on the overdue amount) applied if you fail to pay your EMI by the scheduled due date.
Can I make part payments?: Yes, you can make part payments to reduce your outstanding principal balance, which will lower either your monthly EMI or your remaining tenure.
How does tenure reduction work?: Tenure reduction keeps your monthly EMI amount the same but reduces the remaining months of your loan, saving you more on interest.
How does EMI reduction work?: EMI reduction keeps your remaining tenure the same but lowers your monthly installment amount, reducing your immediate financial burden.
What is a repayment schedule?: A repayment schedule is a table detailing each monthly payment, showing the split between principal and interest, and the outstanding balance.
What is pre EMI interest?: Pre-EMI is the interest charged on the disbursed loan amount before full disbursement and start of regular EMI payments.
Can I pay my EMI using a credit card?: No, banks do not allow you to pay monthly loan installments using a credit card.
What is a standing instruction?: A standing instruction is an authorization given to your bank to automatically transfer the EMI amount from your savings account to your loan account every month.
What happens if my auto debit fails?: If auto-debit fails, you should make a manual payment online immediately to avoid bounce charges and CIBIL score penalties.
Can I pay my EMIs in advance?: Yes, you can pay multiple EMIs in advance if you have excess funds, which will clear your balance faster.
What is the principal component of EMI?: It is the portion of your monthly payment that goes directly toward reducing the actual borrowed loan balance.
What is the interest component of EMI?: It is the portion of your monthly payment that goes toward paying the interest charges for that month.
Why is the interest component higher in: Because interest is calculated on the outstanding balance, which is largest at the start of the loan. As you pay down the principal, the interest component decreases.
Can I choose a weekly repayment schedule: No, retail bank loans are structured strictly on an equated monthly repayment basis.
